findings.reason: The protected app-local and Accepted native sources perform the exact copy-and-bypass operation required by the unusual direct-node contract: copy the guaranteed successor's value, then skip that successor. Two assignments give clear, conventional O(1)-time/O(1)-space behavior, so no candidate is justified.

The app-local function and native class method contain the same value assignment followed by the same pointer assignment. The app-local ListNode definition only supplies LeetCode's injected node model to the standalone runtime.

The legal 8/64/256-node suffix tiers scale the unavailable remainder while keeping the protected mutation constant. The protected source passes at +0.00 relative exponent; a correct implementation that shifts every successor value left before removing the tail passes every output and fails only scaling at +0.34.

The Approach precisely distinguishes deleting an observable list position from detaching the supplied object, proves the suffix transformation, and now labels the non-tail guarantee explicitly. The variant summary states the two actual mutations.
